title: Wan 2.2 5B, node by node, and how it differs from the 14B pair
hook: One small model with a stronger VAE, or two big ones that hand over mid-run. What the configs say, and what our graph changes.

verified.claim: Wan22ImageToVideoLatent makes [1, 48, (n - 1) // 4 + 1, H / 16, W / 16], and uses batch_size only on the branch with a start image.
WAN22_T2V matches model_type t2v with out_dim 48, and is built with image_to_video True.
With a mask, WAN22.process_timestep gives each latent frame its own timestep.
5B: VAE stride (4, 16, 16), dim 3072, 30 layers, sample_shift 5, 50 steps, guide scale 5, 24 fps, 121 frames.
T2V A14B: VAE stride (4, 8, 8), dim 5120, 40 layers, low and high noise checkpoints, boundary 0.875, sample_shift 12, 40 steps, guide scale (3, 4).
The README lists TI2V-5B as high-compression, T2V and I2V, 720P at 24 fps.
Gallery Wan clips have 121 frames with no sound stream.
The graph passes validate_prompt with its file menus skipped.

unchecked: Wan's weights are not on our test machine today, so we did not run this graph for this lesson. Clips are earlier renders from the gallery.
How a 14B file is detected in ComfyUI is inferred from the unet_config match rules. We did not load a 14B file.
The step split on the lab's plain even grid is close to, not the same as, what Wan's own sampler schedule produces.
We did not compare shift 8 and 20 steps against Wan's shift 5 and 50 steps. Our graph's numbers are a studio choice.
